Include: a title/header, the puzzle board (an NxN grid of connector path tiles) with a small Cub token on a start cell and a Star marker on the goal cell, and Run / Reset buttons in a footer. Put strong emphasis on the visual design: make the board the clear focal point, with a warm, playful storybook identity — coherent layout, color, typography, spacing and finish. Make this screen look genuinely beautiful and polished.

history.critique: Brief & Intent: The required footer with Run/Reset is not visible at all — the oversized centered hero (eyebrow + ~90px title + 3-line paragraph) pushes the 6x6 board below the fold, so this does not read as a single game screen and the board, which the brief names the focal point, is actually secondary to the title. The goal star is not visible in the viewport, and the start cell is only a faintly tinted tile, so the core start→goal relationship is unclear. Clarity: connector tiles are ambiguous — most show the same orange 'V' with a small star/flower dot floating above the path, which communicates no direction and adds noise; the Cub token is small and sits on a path without a distinct start treatment, and there are no visible hover/selected states. Visual System: the two floating corner brackets (orange top-left, teal top-right) read as an unfinished frame; cream tiles on a white panel are low-contrast and flat with little depth; the display serif looks like a default Times-like face rather than a crafted storybook voice; the copy promises a 'golden trail' but the path is flat orange. Expressiveness: the identity is warm but the board itself is generic — near-identical tiles, no texture, no character moment — while the distinctive touches (badge, logo, two-tone title) all sit above the fold, leaving the focal board as the least crafted element. Real trade-offs: keeping the large hero title preserves a brand moment but violates 'board is the focal point' and breaks single-screen fit; keeping per-tile stars adds charm but hurts path legibility; the corner brackets are a distinctive idea but currently look broken because only two corners exist in view.
history.suggestion: 1) Reflow to a true single screen: move the wordmark and level badge into a slim top bar, shrink the centered title to a compact masthead (~44–56px) with a one-line subtitle, and size the 6x6 board to fill the remaining viewport so the full grid plus a footer with chunky tactile Run (orange, paw icon) and Reset (outline) buttons are visible without scrolling — the board becomes the largest element on screen. 2) Make the puzzle legible: redraw connectors as clean rounded strokes (straight/corner/T) with consistent width and end caps, remove the per-tile star dots, give the start tile a distinct ring with a larger Cub, and place a clear golden star on the goal tile; shift the path color toward gold to match the 'golden trail' copy. 3) Unify the craft system: one palette (cream paper, golden path, teal accent, brown ink), uniform tile radius with a soft inner shadow for depth, and a complete board frame — either finish the corner brackets on all four corners or replace them with a single stitched/rounded frame; set the title in a rounded system serif stack with the small italic 'n' baseline-aligned. 4) Add storybook life with self-contained CSS only: subtle paper/grass texture in the background, a gentle idle bob on the Cub, tile hover lift + rotate hint, and a solved-state glow on the connected path so Run produces visible feedback.
